### application-core objects O1: an ordinary receiver made by its constructor in the regression and property checks (verification pending)

change `zuwkutwssrpl` · [log `f2a72d8bf772`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/3ba3cc03-2dbc-4a1f-ac36-a1cc13b778a9/f2a72d8bf7720a04a5717514b603a3ed19ed9cec8b05c102d4f439271833eeb0.jsonl.gz)

An instance method of a class that is not a record of primitive components was refused by both equivalence and prove. construction::receiver now makes such a receiver exactly as an object parameter is made (equivalence::made_of, the one usable constructor from primitive leaves and objects made so in turn), named this. In equivalence both versions' receivers must be made the same way; their fields are compared after the call, and this is a new root of the identity relations (harness::Root::Receiver). In prove the target is called on its receiver (invokevirtual) and the assumption, the assertion and the throws clauses read this.f. A receiver outside that is refused by name: a constructor argument that is an array, a String or a dependency says the objects stream builds it; several constructors, a superclass, a cycle, --nullable this, --before-arguments and a correspondence about the receiver are named boundaries.

Verified inline on the native engine with no JBMC: the integration contract's O1 (the throttle's allows verified after construction, one-short refuted and replayed), and five tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs (a receiver's mutation refuted on field:this and run on a JVM, a receiver returned as a copy refuted on identity with this, properties over this.f proved and refuted, the refusals, and cache invalidation by the receiver's constructor). The lib tests and the heap, foundations, compare, effects, application_core, observations, alignment and summaries suites pass. Job 20261108-045000-application-core-objects-o1-lib-tests-in runs lib/tests/integration.rs (JBMC) and examples 190-196, whose kernels recorded Quote#quantity as unresolved for being an instance method.

Found on the way, and not fixed here because proof_cache.rs is the reuse stream's: the regression cache's key doesn't root a version's closure at inner objects' constructors, so a build that changes only an inner constructor reuses another build's proof. That is an unsound hit, which predates this wave. Its reproducer is an ignored test, an_inner_objects_constructor_is_part_of_the_cached_claim, and the stream brief's Progress records it for the reuse stream and the main brief's for-review list.

### application-core objects O1 and O3: a construction plan chooses the constructor, and a setup sequence of one or two calls is checked and replayed as a whole history

change `skvmtlxnuqyw` · [log `62438d21834e`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/3ba3cc03-2dbc-4a1f-ac36-a1cc13b778a9/62438d21834e0f7e53152a008ab6119d60b2d964ca39c10365a53adcc778f03b.jsonl.gz)

equivalence --plan, prove --plan and a planned claim (spec::heap::check) now make their inputs by the plan: construction::root builds each root by the constructor descriptor its node names, which is how one of several constructors is chosen. construction::setup_calls gives one or two void calls on the receiver, which the regression harness calls in both versions before the target. A setup call that throws ends that version's history, and its exception, a category of its step's own, is the outcome compared, so an input one version's setup rejects is a difference and is never dropped. The property harness skips such a history, as it skips a rejected construction. The interpreter replay runs the history, the JVM run gets it by running the harness, and the witness reads 'allows(this=new Throttle(...), n=...), after the setup this.take(setup.0.n=...)'. The statement gains the setup assumption and setupCalls; a planned claim's result names its label and restrictions; the domain gate compares a plan's classes with the claim's. What a plan can't make yet is refused by its stream's name: arrays, nullable or shared nodes, factories, dependencies, adapted values, setup calls that return a value, more than two setup calls, plans that differ between versions. A setup claim runs uncached (its key wouldn't root the setup methods), and prove --cache --plan is refused (the property key doesn't read the plan).

Verified inline, native engine and no JBMC: four new tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs. (1) O3 on the frozen throttle claims, with only their allocation bound raised to 1: after-setup is verified with no setup, labelled for that domain, and refuted after one take, the whole history in the witness and run on a JVM; one-short is refuted and after verified under both claims. (2) A plan choosing one of Window's two constructors, verified and refuted, with a missing constructor and a misnamed leaf refused. (3) A setup rejection in one version only, refuted on exception. (4) prove over the states one setup call reaches. The lib tests, heap (its Phase 0 placeholder test for a planned domain now checks the plan instead), foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill all pass.

Found, and recorded for the coordinator under the brief's Progress: the frozen throttle claims bound allocations at 0, while allows and take each allocate the IllegalArgumentException they throw. Now that plans are checked, the allocation gate counts it, so the contract's O3 (tests/application_core.rs) is unresolved where expected.json says verified or refuted, and the integration check fails on O3 until the fixture is corrected. The gate is left as it is. Interface requests to reuse (root setup methods in the regression key; read the plan in the property key and in spec::cache::key) and to the coordinator (a setup field in witness::Call and its stored form; a plan input for compare) are recorded too. No new job: the harness changes apply only to layouts with setup calls, which no example or JBMC test has; the pending job 20261108-045000-application-core-objects-o1-lib-tests-in still covers the integration tests and examples 190-196.

### application-core objects O1 and O2: a constructor may take a bounded primitive array, kept apart between the versions, and a leaked defensive copy is refuted

change `rukolrmuswxn` · [log `6165fac44ea7`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/3ba3cc03-2dbc-4a1f-ac36-a1cc13b778a9/6165fac44ea742c036f028b896813199c92f3f4adfc53dd9caa16c2a7c0088ed.jsonl.gz)

A construction's leaves are now primitives or arrays of integral or boolean elements (harness::is_leaf), with a plan or without one (equivalence::made_of), so a receiver or parameter such as Buffer(int[] data) needs no adapter of the application's. The previous version's object is made from the harness's copy of the array, so the two versions' heaps are apart, while within a version the object and the caller share the array the caller passed. The caller's array is compared after the call (array:this.data), in the harness and in the interpreter replay. The domain says each array of the construction is bounded, not null and its own, and construction::stated_bounds states the array bound, which the shared Domain::has_arrays doesn't see for an array inside an object. A plan's array values are roots or constructor arguments; their max_length must equal the check's array bound, and a null array or one value given at two paths is refused by name. A property's expressions still can't read an object's array field, refused by name as before.

Verified inline (native engine, no JBMC), with three new tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs. A Buffer receiver: total rewritten is verified and a defect refuted and run on a JVM; a rewrite of bump, which writes into the receiver's own array, is verified, which it wouldn't be if both versions shared the array; prove verifies size() &lt;= 3 and refutes total() >= 0. O2's negative control: a constructor that keeps the caller's array where the previous version copied it is refuted on array:this.data alone, the receivers' fields agreeing, replayed on a JVM. A plan's array leaf is checked, and a mismatched bound and a null array are refused. The lib tests and every inline suite pass, except the contract's O3, which still fails on the frozen throttle claims' allocation bound recorded in the previous commit. No job: apart from the quote fixture's QuoteRequest, whose String argument is still refused, no example or fixture class has a constructor that takes a primitive array, so no example's result changes.

### application-core objects O2: a plan's root may be null or one of other roots' objects, one node at two roots is one object, and two parameters that were one object becoming distinct is refuted

change `xnwtzpszzxsv` · [log `199b094cac38`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/3ba3cc03-2dbc-4a1f-ac36-a1cc13b778a9/199b094cac380c9ae68cca59703fc5f55b73076ca372cb615298b8ba8d6dc063.jsonl.gz)

A construction plan's root node may now be null (nullable) or one of the objects of other roots (same_as), each a boolean flag of the harness made as --nullable and --may-alias make it, and one node at two roots is one object, always, with no flag: harness::Choice::always, set by Layout::share and honoured by both harnesses' bytecode and source, by Layout::made (so the witness, the interpreter replay and the JVM run of the harness), and by the domain ('b: the same object as a'). Both versions' plans must make the same choices, so that their identity relations start alike. Inside a nested object a choice or a shared node stays refused by name, as do a shared node with a choice besides, a same_as naming no root's node, and a nullable receiver.

Verified inline on the native engine without JBMC: new unit tests in construction and harness, and four tests in lib/tests/application_core_objects.rs. The negative control of O2: a rewrite of twice(a, b) that keeps its first read of b is verified over two nodes and refuted over one node and over a same_as choice, the witness naming b as the same object as a, replayed in the interpreter and run on a JVM. Also: identity of the result with a shared node, a nullable root refuting a dropped null check, and a property over a shared node. The lib tests (228) and the suites heap, foundations, compare, effects, observations, alignment, summaries, conformance and skill pass; application_core passes except O3, which still waits on the frozen throttle claims' allocation bound recorded for the coordinator in the brief's Progress. No job: no example or JBMC test has a plan with a shared node.
